summary: Store.RecordProviderFact (internal/store/peloton.go) always advances fetched_at to now on a successful fetch, even when the content-hash short-circuit determines the payload is byte-identical to what's already stored and skips rewriting it. fetched_at means "when was this record last confirmed fresh against the live API," not "when did its content last change" -- those are different questions, and only the second one is answered by a content-hash comparison. The payload-rewrite skip itself is preserved as a write-avoidance optimization; only the timestamp update was added to the unchanged-content branch. Any future regen or edit to this function must preserve advancing fetched_at unconditionally on every successful call, or any consumer that treats fetched_at as a freshness/staleness signal (e.g. sync's --stale-before, sync-stale-before-backfill.json) breaks silently for records whose live content happens to not have changed.
reason: Discovered live while implementing and testing --stale-before (NEW ISSUE E, fourth live post-fix verification sweep): a --stale-before refetch of a real record whose live content genuinely hadn't changed left fetched_at completely untouched, because RecordProviderFact's content-hash dedup returned early without touching the row at all. This meant the same record would be reported stale on every subsequent --stale-before call forever, never actually clearing its stale status -- silently defeating the entire feature for any record whose backfill happens to not change the stored bytes (which will be common: not every workout in a --stale-before range is actually affected by whatever fix motivated the backfill).
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck all green. New test TestRecordProviderFact_AdvancesFetchedAtEvenWhenContentUnchanged confirms fetched_at strictly advances on a second RecordProviderFact call with byte-identical content, while the returned "changed" bool still correctly reports false. Live-verified against the user's real account as part of the --stale-before verification: before this fix, two real performance records refetched via --stale-before kept their original (stale) fetched_at despite being successfully re-fetched; after this fix, both correctly advanced to the current time and a repeat --stale-before call correctly reported already_up_to_date instead of reprocessing them again.
